title: Next fire time for cron expressions
spec:
The repository is empty. Create `cron.py` with `next_fire(expr, after)`: given a 5-field cron expression and a naive `datetime.datetime` `after`, return the earliest naive `datetime` strictly later than `after` whose second and microsecond are 0 and which the expression matches. No time zones or DST: treat datetimes as plain calendar values (Gregorian calendar, `datetime` range).

Expression syntax:
- Exactly 5 fields separated by one or more spaces/tabs (leading/trailing whitespace ignored): minute (0-59), hour (0-23), day-of-month (1-31), month (1-12), day-of-week (0-7, where both 0 and 7 mean Sunday, 1 = Monday ... 6 = Saturday).
- A field is a comma-separated list of one or more items. An item is one of: `*` (the field's whole range; for day-of-week that is 0-7), `N` (a single value), `A-B` (inclusive range, A <= B required; no wrap-around), optionally followed by `/S` on any of these forms: `*/S` and `A-B/S` take every S-th value of the range starting at its first value; `N/S` means `N-max/S` where max is the field's maximum (e.g. minute `5/20` = 5,25,45). S is an integer >= 1 (it may exceed the range size, e.g. minute `*/90` = 0).
- Values are decimal digit strings (no signs). In the month field the names JAN..DEC, and in the day-of-week field the names SUN..SAT, may be used anywhere a number can (including as range ends, e.g. `MON-FRI`, `JAN-MAR/2`); names are case-insensitive and are not allowed in any other field.
- A time matches when its minute, hour and month are in their fields and its day matches. Day rule: a day-of-month or day-of-week field is *unrestricted* exactly when its text is the single character `*` (so `*/2` or `1-31` count as restricted). If both are restricted, the day matches when EITHER the day-of-month OR the day-of-week matches. Otherwise only the restricted one (if any) must match.

Errors: raise `ValueError` for any malformed expression: wrong number of fields, empty items, unknown names or names in the wrong field, values out of range, reversed ranges, steps that are not integers >= 1, or any other text not described above. Also raise `ValueError` for a well-formed expression that can never fire on any date (e.g. `0 0 30 2 *`, `0 0 31 4,6 *`). Raising when `next_fire` is called is enough.

Performance: every call must return within 50 ms even when the answer is years away (e.g. `0 0 29 2 *` asked on 2097-03-01 must return 2104-02-29 00:00, because 2100 is not a leap year). Iterating minute by minute is too slow.

Add unit tests runnable with `python3 -m unittest -q`.
acceptance: next_fire returns the earliest matching minute strictly after `after`
lists, ranges, steps, names and Sunday as 0 or 7 work in every combination
day-of-month/day-of-week OR rule applies exactly when both fields are restricted
leap years, month lengths and year rollover are handled; calls are fast
malformed or never-firing expressions raise ValueError
